import numpy as np

def make_data():
    return np.array([[1, 2], [1.5, 1.8], [2, 2.5], [5, 6], [5.5, 5.5], [6, 6.2]])

def test_kmeans_basic():
    X = make_data()
    labels, centroids = exercise.kmeans_cluster(X)
    assert isinstance(labels, list), f"Expected list for labels, got {type(labels)}"
    assert isinstance(centroids, list), f"Expected list for centroids, got {type(centroids)}"
    assert len(labels) == 6, f"Expected 6 labels, got {len(labels)}"
    assert len(centroids) == 2, f"Expected 2 centroids, got {len(centroids)}"
    assert all(label in (0, 1) for label in labels), f"Labels should be 0 or 1, got {labels}"
    assert labels[:3] == [0, 0, 0], f"First 3 points should be cluster 0, got {labels[:3]}"
    assert labels[3:] == [1, 1, 1], f"Last 3 points should be cluster 1, got {labels[3:]}"

def test_centroids_shape():
    X = make_data()
    _, centroids = exercise.kmeans_cluster(X)
    assert len(centroids[0]) == 2, f"Each centroid should have 2 coordinates, got {centroids[0]}"
    c0_x = centroids[0][0]
    c0_y = centroids[0][1]
    assert 1.0 <= c0_x <= 2.5, f"First centroid x should be around 1.5, got {c0_x}"
    assert 1.5 <= c0_y <= 2.5, f"First centroid y should be around 2.1, got {c0_y}"

def test_kmeans_k_equals_3():
    X = make_data()
    labels, centroids = exercise.kmeans_cluster(X, k=3)
    assert len(labels) == 6, f"Expected 6 labels, got {len(labels)}"
    assert len(centroids) == 3, f"Expected 3 centroids, got {len(centroids)}"

def test_different_data():
    X = np.array([[0, 0], [0, 1], [1, 0], [10, 10], [10, 11], [11, 10]])
    labels, centroids = exercise.kmeans_cluster(X)
    assert len(labels) == 6, f"Expected 6 labels, got {len(labels)}"
    assert len(centroids) == 2, f"Expected 2 centroids, got {len(centroids)}"

def test_labels_as_ints():
    X = make_data()
    labels, _ = exercise.kmeans_cluster(X)
    for i, label in enumerate(labels):
        assert isinstance(label, (int, np.integer)), f"Label at index {i} should be int, got {type(label)}"

solution_code:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

def predict_cluster(X, new_point, k=2, random_state=42):
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=random_state, n_init=10)
    kmeans.fit(X)
    pred = kmeans.predict(new_point)
    return int(pred[0])
